What if instead of being bumped away, you stick then get caught by the wheel?

This may seem stupid at first glance, but it would probably cause much less severe injuries than being thrown only to crash into the ground just as hard a second time. Maybe if they combined this with an external airbag that was covered in the sticky material and deployed if the car senses an imminent impact it would be a really significant improvement.

I'm not so sure. Take the position of the person in that thumbnail, for example. Let's say the car originally lost control by hitting a patch of black ice. In the original scenario, the pedestrian would simply be thrown from the collision site. Now, they're glued to the front of the car, as it continues careening down the road, as the new hood ornament, destined to take any front-end impacts before the car does. And god forbid should it be something like a building or guard rail that brings that car to a stop. You could easily survive being thrown from the impact of a collision. But having 3,000 lbs of fiberglass, steel, glass, and aluminum plow into you from behind as you slam into a building at 30-40 MPH? A snowball has a better chance on Miami Beach on a sunny day.

It's about statistics, if the number of cases where a car hits a person and then hits a wall isn't greater than the number of cases where a car hits a person and then doesn't hit anything else it would overall reduce deaths to have sticky cars.

Also this is specifically for self driving cars, which will be many times more skilled than any human at avoiding static obstacles and maintain control even after an accident.
